questions.t: row major and column major form of an array
questions.q: int M[4][6] is stored in row-major order starting at address 1000, with sizeof(int) = 4 bytes. What is the address of M[2][3]?
questions.model: Row-major offset = (2 x 6 + 3) x 4 = 60 bytes; address = 1000 + 60 = 1060.

questions.q: What does strcmp("apple", "banana") return in C?
opts: The length of the shorter string
questions.model: strcmp returns a negative value when the first string sorts before the second ('a' < 'b').

questions.q: Write a C function void transpose(int a[3][3], int t[3][3]) that stores the transpose of a in t, and a main() that prints the transpose of a matrix read from the user.
double d[10]; double *p = d; If d starts at address 5000 and sizeof(double) = 8, what address does p + 3 hold?
questions.model: Pointer arithmetic scales by the element size: 5000 + 3 x 8 = 5024.

questions.q: Write a C function that swaps two integers in the caller using pointers (call by reference), and show how it is called.
Compare malloc(), calloc() and realloc(): what each allocates, how memory is initialised, and when you would use each.
questions.model: malloc(size) allocates uninitialised bytes; calloc(n, size) allocates n elements and zero-initialises them; realloc(p, size) resizes an existing block, possibly moving it. Use calloc when zeroed memory is needed, realloc to grow a buffer, malloc otherwise.

questions.t: Dangling, Void, Null and Wild pointers
questions.q: Read the assertion and reason about dangling, Void, Null and Wild pointers and choose the correct option.
questions.assertion: After free(p); the pointer p becomes a dangling pointer.
questions.reason: free() sets p to NULL automatically.
questions.model: A is true: p still holds the address of released memory. R is false: free() does not change p; the programmer should set p = NULL.

questions.q: Define a self-referential structure for a student record (roll number, name, next) and write C code that builds a linked list of n students read from the user using dynamic memory allocation, then prints it.
questions.model: struct student { int roll; char name[30]; struct student *next; }; Loop n times: node = malloc(sizeof *node); read fields; node->next = NULL; append via tail pointer. Traverse from head printing each node; free nodes at the end.

questions.q: Which fopen() mode opens an existing text file for both reading and writing without truncating it?
questions.model: "r+" opens an existing file for reading and writing; "w+" truncates; "a" appends only.

questions.t: counting lines in a text file
questions.q: Write a C program that counts the number of lines in a text file whose name is given by the user, handling the case where the file cannot be opened.
Explain the roles of fseek(), ftell() and rewind() in random file access, with the meaning of SEEK_SET, SEEK_CUR and SEEK_END.
questions.model: fseek(fp, offset, origin) moves the file position relative to SEEK_SET (start), SEEK_CUR (current) or SEEK_END (end); ftell(fp) returns the current position; rewind(fp) returns to the start and clears the error indicator.

questions.t: Reading and writing in a binary file
questions.q: True or False: fwrite() writes the in-memory bytes of a structure to a binary file, so the file can be read back with fread() into the same structure type.
questions.model: True. fwrite/fread copy raw bytes, so the same structure layout reads back correctly on the same platform.

questions.q: State three features of Python that make it suitable for rapid problem solving, and contrast one of them with C.
questions.model: Interpreted, dynamically typed, rich standard library, readable indentation-based syntax. Example: Python variables need no type declarations, whereas C requires declaring types before use.

questions.q: In Python, a block of statements is defined by its ___, not by braces, and a single-line comment starts with the ___ character.
questions.model: Blocks are defined by indentation; comments start with #.

questions.q: What is the value of the Python expression (12 & 10) | (5 << 1) ?
What is the result of the Python expression 7 // 2 + 7 % 2 * 2.0 ?
What is printed by the Python statement print(sum(range(3, 20, 4)))?
Write a Python function is_prime(n) and use it to print all prime numbers between 1 and 100. Explain why checking divisors up to the square root of n is sufficient.
Write a Python program that copies the contents of source.txt to dest.txt line by line using with statements.
For the case, propose a Python solution using if-elif-else and loops, and evaluate whether a dictionary of slabs would be a better design than a long if-elif chain.
questions.case: An electricity board charges Rs 3 per unit for the first 100 units, Rs 5 per unit for the next 100 units and Rs 8 per unit above 200 units. A clerk enters the units consumed by each of several consumers until a negative value is entered and needs the bill for each.
questions.model: Loop reading units until negative; compute bill with if-elif-else on the slabs (e.g. 250 units = 300 + 500 + 400 = 1200). A table of (limit, rate) slabs iterated in a loop is easier to change than hard-coded branches, at the cost of slightly more abstract code; for frequently revised tariffs the table is better.
